To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
n-grams of length 2 and 3 are more effective than longer n-grams in plagiarism detection.

(1) the best results for plagiarism detection based on n-grams comparisons are obtained for n = 2 and n = 3; (2) n-grams of length 2 are more suitable than those of length 3; (3) the best results are achieved for a window size of 5; and (4) the results are better for the METER corpus when considering the original texts as the reference corpus.
n-gram comparison is an effective technique to detect plagiarism in texts.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) the definition of a plagiarism model that considers the different types of plagiarism, (2) the definition of the best comparison units for the suspicious and original text fragments, and (3) the evaluation of the plagiarism detection performance.
the following aspects: - The definition of proper n-gram size to be used for plagiarism detection.
the following questions: (1) What are the best n-grams to use in plagiarism detection?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the n-gram approach is the best one for plagiarism detection in general, and in particular, for detecting plagiarised fragments that are modified from the original text.
the n-gram based method is the best method to detect plagiarised fragments.
the best results for the automatic plagiarism detection task are obtained when using n-grams of low level (n = 2 and 3) and a large number of reference documents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
n-grams comparison is a good alternative for the automatic plagiarism detection of texts that have undergone modifications.
the most effective approach is to use n-gram comparisons for the automatic detection of plagiarism, and to consider low level n-grams for this kind of applications.

the most effective approach for plagiarism detection is to use a combination of low level n-grams comparisons, and to consider the results from the most frequent and the less frequent n-grams separately.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of n-grams as comparison units is a promising approach for the detection of modified text chunks.
the best performance in plagiarism detection is obtained when the comparison units are small enough to capture the smallest changes between the source and the suspicious texts.
, when dealing with short texts, the best approach to plagiarism detection is the use of low level word ngrams.
